USA.name: USA
USA.rationale: Mature mass-production, semiconductor, mainframe, aerospace and nuclear industries. Operational F-4, F-111, B-52, AH-1G, strategic missiles and nuclear submarines predate the cutoff. Operational equipment does not imply every 1970 prototype or every future module.
exclusions: No all-1970 package, flying-wing combat airframe, later pulse-Doppler step, laser-guided weapons1972 or postwar IFV type merely because a prototype existed.
No special project completion, warheads, satellites, equipment or deployed formations are created.

CAN.name: Canada
CAN.rationale: Domestic aerospace, electronics and civil nuclear engineering coexist with licensed Canadian-built CF-104/J79, imported CF-101 and British diesel submarines. NPD1962 and DouglasPoint1966/68 demonstrate actual heavy-water engineering; MD has no accurately dated pre1970 CANDU power node, so do not substitute Magnox or PWR.
exclusions: No sovereign nuclear weapons, ICBMs, nuclear submarine design, orbital launcher or later CF-18.
CANDU power representation is limited by the existing tree; no forced 1971 mutually exclusive policy choice.

AST.name: Australia
AST.rationale: Licensed MirageIIIO assembly and established shipyards; HIFAR1958 is research-only. Perth guided-missile destroyers and Oberon-class diesel submarines precede1970. F-111 and leasedF-4 deliveries are later than the cutoff.
exclusions: No F-111, F-4, nuclear power station, indigenous strategic missile or nuclear submarine.
Mirage operation does not grant indigenous semiconductor or jet-engine research.

NZL.name: New Zealand
NZL.rationale: Established engineering, hydroelectricity and maintenance of imported Vampire/Canberra aircraft, Hercules, Orion and Iroquois. Skyhawks were handed over and shipped only during1970.
exclusions: No January1970 Skyhawk, supersonic fighter, nuclear programme or submarine industry.

ARG.name: Argentina
ARG.rationale: Industrial and university base with domestic small arms, vehicles and limited aircraft development; RA-1 locally constructed1958. PulquiII never entered series service, Pucara was a1969 prototype. Operational combat aviation remains imported/subsonic.
exclusions: No MirageIII1972, Pucara series-production1975, TAM tank or Atucha commercial power1974.
No automatic PWR/Magnox from a research reactor.

BRA.name: Brazil
BRA.rationale: Substantial industrial and engineering base, licensed small arms and motor vehicles, Meteor-era jets and embryonic Embraer1969. Research reactors operated by1957/1965; nuclear power and modern supersonic combat aviation came later.
exclusions: No MirageIII1972, F-5delivery1975, EMB110service1973, Angra power or nuclear submarine.
No universal agricultural high-yield research from founding EMBRAPA1973.

MEX.name: Mexico
MEX.rationale: Import-substitution industry and military workshops; imported T-33-era aviation. TRIGA reactor acceptedNov/Dec1968. The Mexican wheat programme demonstrates established high-yield agricultural knowledge before1968.
exclusions: No F-5, power reactor, nuclear fuel fabrication, domestic jet design or modern MBT production.

CUB.name: Cuba
CUB.rationale: Soviet-supported operating and maintenance capacity includes MiG21, Soviet medium tanks and SAMs. Plantation and processing industries do not imply Soviet industrial, semiconductor or strategic research capabilities.
exclusions: No Cuban ownership of Soviet strategic missiles or nuclear weapons after their1962 withdrawal.
No indigenous supersonic design/engine, submarine industry or nuclear power.

PRU.name: Peru
PRU.rationale: Mirage5P arrivedJune1968 and flew locallyJuly1968, justifying imported supersonic operating knowledge. Civil industry and field forces remain uneven and predominantly supplied from abroad.
exclusions: No later Soviet tank/fighter imports, domestic Mirage development or reactor1988.

CHL.name: Chile
CHL.rationale: Copper-linked processing, public engineering and imported military equipment. Operational Hunter fleet1967/68 is early-jet knowledge; a supersonic dive is not a sustained supersonic fighter design. The first research reactor followed1974.
exclusions: No Mirage/F-5, indigenous supersound design, reactor1974 or PWR power plant.

COL.name: Colombia
COL.rationale: Industry and financial mainframe use existed, including imported IBM650 in1957 and banking data processing1969. Imported computing supports only basic use, not an indigenous integrated-circuit industry. IAN-R1 research-reactor operation from1965 supports nuclear science only.
exclusions: No modern supersonic fighter, semiconductor industry, MBT production or civil power reactor.
Research reactor knowledge grants no actual enrichment plant, power reactor or nuclear weapon.

BOL.name: Bolivia
BOL.rationale: Conservative land and piston-aircraft maintenance baseline. The Bolivian air force records first T-33 arrivals on7Aug1973, so an early-jet starting grant would be premature.
exclusions: No T-33/F-86, nuclear reactor, modern tank production or modern naval shipbuilding.

VEN.name: Venezula
VEN.rationale: Oil industry and service workshops support modern construction, but US-supplied F-86-era jets do not establish a domestic aerospace sector. Mirage deliveries and advanced naval programmes belong later. RV-1 research reactor first critical12July1960 supports nuclear science only.
exclusions: Conservative capability inference; the cited regional surveys do not prove every individual technology.
No strategic nuclear, missile, semiconductor or modern aircraft-design package.
Research reactor knowledge grants no actual enrichment plant, power reactor or nuclear weapon.
